query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Analyze and triage Zendesk support tickets at scale: search ticket queues, enrich tickets with requester/order context, add private AI triage notes and tags, verify queues are drained, and aggregate product-support trends over a large historical ticket set.
query_ground_truth.query: search support ticket queues and retrieve ticket details
query_ground_truth.rationale: Searching queues and fetching specific tickets are core retrieval operations needed to triage and analyze support tickets at scale.

request.query: search support ticket queues and retrieve ticket details

results.use_case: search support ticket queues and retrieve ticket details
results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if scoping to a specific organization)] [Prerequisite]: Resolve the target organization context using FRESHDESK_GET_COMPANIES (to narrow ticket retrieval).
[Optional (if building advanced filters)] [Prerequisite]: Inspect available/searchable ticket fields using FRESHDESK_LIST_TICKET_FIELDS (to form valid search queries).
[Required] [Step]: Find matching tickets using FRESHDESK_GET_SEARCH (return key fields like subject/status/created time); iterate all pages to avoid partial results.
[Required] [Next Step]: For each ticket of interest, fetch full details plus response-time metrics using FRESHDESK_VIEW_TICKET (include stats to get first-response timing).

[Optional (if FRESHDESK_GET_SEARCH is unavailable or returns unusable results)] [Fallback]: Pull a broader ticket list using FRESHDESK_GET_TICKETS, filter client-side, then call FRESHDESK_VIEW_TICKET per ticket to obtain stats.
[Optional (if ticket_type_id unknown)] [Prerequisite]: Discover candidate ticket types using INTERCOM_LIST_TICKET_TYPES (map name/category to id).
[Optional (if filtering by ticket state)] [Prerequisite]: Discover valid states using INTERCOM_LIST_TICKET_STATES (ensure the state value you plan to filter is supported).
[Optional (if multiple similar types or unclear schema)] [Next Step]: Validate the chosen type using INTERCOM_GET_TICKET_TYPE (confirm attributes/states before searching).
[Required] [Step]: Search tickets using INTERCOM_SEARCH_TICKETS (filter by ticket_type_id and the intended time field, e.g., created_at/updated_at, in epoch seconds).
[Required] [Step]: Paginate results using INTERCOM_SEARCH_TICKETS (loop with data.pages.next.starting_after until data.pages.next is null; aggregate and dedupe by ticket id).
[Optional (if search payload lacks needed fields)] [Next Step]: Enrich specific results using INTERCOM_GET_TICKET (fetch full ticket details by id).

[Fallback (if INTERCOM_SEARCH_TICKETS returns total_count=0 unexpectedly)] [Fallback]: Re-check ticket_type_id/states via INTERCOM_GET_TICKET_TYPE or INTERCOM_LIST_TICKET_STATES, widen the window/confirm epoch seconds, then retry INTERCOM_SEARCH_TICKETS.
known_pitfalls: [FRESHDESK_VIEW_TICKET] Response-time/first-response metrics live under a nested stats object; list-style endpoints may omit them unless you expand per ticket.
[FRESHDESK_GET_SEARCH] Payload shape returns matches under response.data.results rather than a top-level tickets array, so parsing must follow that structure.
[FRESHDESK_LIST_TICKET_FIELDS] Search filters rely on internal field keys (not display labels); using the wrong key can yield empty/incorrect search results.
[FRESHDESK_GET_TICKETS] Listing tickets may not include the timing metrics needed for SLA/first-response reporting, so plan on FRESHDESK_VIEW_TICKET for final numbers.
[INTERCOM_LIST_TICKET_TYPES] Large workspaces can return very large lists; filter programmatically rather than manually scanning.
[INTERCOM_SEARCH_TICKETS] Time filters are epoch seconds; passing milliseconds can silently shift the effective date range.
[INTERCOM_SEARCH_TICKETS] Pagination is cursor-based via data.pages.next.starting_after (not page numbers); stopping early misses results.
[INTERCOM_SEARCH_TICKETS] Valid queries can return tickets=[] and total_count=0; confirm you used the intended timestamp field (created_at vs updated_at) before concluding there are no matches.
[INTERCOM_SEARCH_TICKETS] Re-running overlapping ranges without deduping by ticket id can inflate totals and produce duplicates.

FRESHDESK_GET_SEARCH.description: Tool to search and filter tickets in Freshdesk using flexible query syntax. Use when you need to find tickets based on status, priority, tags, custom fields, dates, or other ticket attributes with complex filtering logic.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Starts at 1 and cannot exceed 10. Default: 1. Each page returns up to 30 results. Maximum 300 tickets can be retrieved across all pages.

query.description: Query string to filter tickets using field:value syntax. Wrap conditions in parentheses for grouping. Use AND, OR for logic. Use :> (≥) and :< (≤) for numeric/date comparisons. Use null for empty fields. String values need single quotes. Do NOT include outer double quotes - they are added automatically. Max 512 characters. Common searchable fields: status (2=Open, 3=Pending, 4=Resolved, 5=Closed), priority (1=Low, 2=Medium, 3=High, 4=Urgent), agent_id, group_id, tag, created_at, updated_at, due_by. Custom fields use cf_ prefix. Note: Not all fields are searchable (e.g., requester_id may not work); use FRESHDESK_LIST_TICKET_FIELDS to discover available searchable fields. Dates in UTC (YYYY-MM-DD).

FRESHDESK_VIEW_TICKET.description: Views an existing ticket in Freshdesk. Ticket details are returned nested under `response_data` in the tool response.

include.description: Comma-separated list of additional information to include in the response. Valid values: 'stats' (ticket timing statistics like first response time), 'requester' (full requester details), 'company' (company information). Example: 'stats,requester,company' to include all expansion fields.

ticket_id.description: ID of the ticket to be viewed

INTERCOM_SEARCH_TICKETS.description: Tool to search tickets in Intercom by filtering attribute values. Use when you need to find tickets matching specific criteria like state, creation date, assignment, or custom attributes.

field.description: The searchable attribute for simple queries (e.g., created_at, ticket_state_id, open)

value.description: For simple queries: single value or array. For complex queries: array of filter objects with field/operator/value

operator.description: Logical operator for combining multiple filters: AND or OR. Required when using multiple filters in value array

query.description: Query object containing filters to search tickets. Can be simple (single field/value) or complex (AND/OR with multiple filters)

per_page.description: Number of results per page (default: 20, max: 150)

starting_after.description: Cursor for pagination - use to fetch the next page of results

FRESHDESK_GET_TICKETS.description: Retrieves a list of tickets from Freshdesk. Tickets are returned under `response_data` in the response object.

filter.description: Predefined filter to apply. Possible values include 'new_and_my_open', 'watching', 'spam', 'deleted', etc.

sort_by.description: Field to sort tickets by, e.g., 'created_at'

created_since.description: Retrieve tickets created since this timestamp. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ
